title: Your own story
job: An eight-sentence account, built from the whole ladder
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Wenn ich + Konj-II + , + würde ich + V-inf

rules.text: The format: each item here is an ACCOUNT of at most eight sentences — L2-M10's four grown up — and the word bound applies to each sentence inside it, not to the item. Eight is a ceiling, not a target; four good sentences are an account. The new-word spend is as close to nothing as the format allows, and that is the point: everything a story of yours needs has already been taught, and a sentence that wants a new noun is a sentence that wants rewriting.

THREE PASTS NOW SHARE ONE ACCOUNT, and each has a job the other two cannot do. The PERFEKT moves the story along — auxiliary second, participle last (L2-M10). The PRÄTERITUM holds its states, and only for the verbs that prefer it: war, waren, hatte, hatten (L1-M5), konnte and wollte (L2-M10). The PLUSQUAMPERFEKT (L3-M5) is the step further back, for what had already happened when the story starts: Ich hatte schon gearbeitet, als er angerufen hat.

WORD ORDER is the real exit test, because an account is the only place where every law in the course collides at once: the verb second under a fronted time (L1-M4, L2-M6), the bracket around a modal or an auxiliary (L2-M1, L2-M10), the verb last in every subordinate clause (L1-M9), the fronted subordinate clause with the two verbs meeting across the comma (L3-M3), and the separable prefix stranded at the end (L3-M1). Get all five right inside eight sentences and the level is passed.

The checklist of what this level lets a story carry that four sentences could not: a reason with weil (L1-M9), a concession with obwohl (L3-M3), a condition or a regret in Konjunktiv II (L3-M4), a line of what somebody said with no backshift (L3-M5), a feeling that is reflexive (L3-M6), a noun phrase with a declined adjective inside it (L3-M2), and als for the one past moment the story turns on (L2-M9's word, L3-M5's rule). That list is the difference between a timetable and a story.

What stays out, so the level ends at a known edge: the past counterfactual (wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte) is L4-M3, the Konjunktiv I of reported speech is L4-M7, the past passive and the agent named with von are L4-M7, the narrative Präteritum beyond L1-M5's and L2-M10's handful of verbs is L4-M8, and the time clauses with bevor, während, seitdem and bis are L4-M6. Nothing here needs any of them.

The register the level ends on: tell the same story to a friend and to a stranger, du and Sie, and nothing else about it changes — the verbs, the order and the tenses all stay put. That is where L2-M1 began, and the whole ladder above it has been one address away the entire time.

sentences.display: Gestern hatte ich schon gearbeitet, als mein Chef angerufen hat. Ich war müde. Trotzdem bin ich ins Büro gefahren. Schließlich habe ich alles gemacht
sentences.cue: Yesterday I had already worked when my boss rang. I was tired. I drove to the office anyway. In the end I did everything
sentences.literal: yesterday had I already worked, when my boss called has. I was tired. nevertheless am I into-the office driven. finally have I everything done

words.note: alles is singular and takes a singular verb: Alles ist gut. It is the neuter partner of L3-M9's plural alle.

sentences.trap: All three pasts are in one account here and none of them is interchangeable: hatte gearbeitet happened first, hat angerufen second, war holds the state across both.
sentences.sound: GES-tern HAT-uh ikh shone guh-AR-buy-tet, als mine shef AN-guh-roo-fen hat. ikh var MUE-duh. TROTS-daym bin ikh ins bue-ROH guh-FAH-ren. SHLEES-likh HAH-buh ikh AL-es guh-MAKHT.
sentences.usage: The shape of a day recounted to a colleague the next morning.
sentences.mnemonic: Perfekt moves it, Präteritum holds it, Plusquamperfekt goes back one more.

sentences.display: Heute bin ich wieder früh aufgestanden. Danach habe ich meine Freundin angerufen. Weil sie Zeit hatte, sind wir zusammen ins Kino gegangen. Es war schön
sentences.cue: Today I got up early again. Then I rang my friend. Because she had time, we went to the cinema together. It was lovely
sentences.literal: today am I again early up-stood. after-that have I my friend called. because she time had, are we together into-the cinema gone. it was lovely

words.note: wieder sits in the middle of the sentence, never at the front of the account: Ich bin wieder früh aufgestanden. Not the same as noch einmal, which is one more time.

sentences.trap: The weil clause is fronted, so its verb goes last and the main clause's verb comes straight after the comma: hatte, sind — two verbs meeting across it.
sentences.sound: HOY-tuh bin ikh VEE-der frue OWF-guh-shtan-den. dah-NAKH HAH-buh ikh MY-nuh FROYN-din AN-guh-roo-fen. vile zee tsite HAT-uh, zint veer tsoo-ZAM-en ins KEE-noh guh-GANG-en. es var shoen.
sentences.usage: The friendly version of what you did today, told to somebody who asked.

sentences.display: Obwohl ich krank war, bin ich zur Arbeit gefahren. Ich wäre lieber zu Hause geblieben. Eigentlich war das nicht gut
sentences.cue: Although I was ill, I went to work. I'd rather have stayed at home. That wasn't really a good idea
sentences.literal: although I ill was, am I to-the work driven. I would-be rather at home stayed. actually was that not good

words.note: eigentlich softens what follows and quietly says the opposite was true: Eigentlich war das nicht gut. It is a comment on the sentence, not on a word in it.

sentences.trap: obwohl opens a subordinate clause, so war goes to the end of it — and then the main clause starts with its own verb, bin.
sentences.sound: op-VOLE ikh krank var, bin ikh tsoor AR-bite guh-FAH-ren. ikh VAY-ruh LEE-ber tsoo HOW-zuh guh-BLEE-ben. EYE-gent-likh var das nikht goot.
sentences.usage: Owning up to a decision, in the register you would use with a colleague.

sentences.display: Mein Kollege hat gesagt, dass er den Vertrag unterschrieben hat. Ich habe gefragt, ob es ein Problem gibt. Er hat nur geantwortet, dass er keine Zeit hat
sentences.cue: My colleague said he had signed the contract. I asked whether there was a problem. He only answered that he had no time
sentences.literal: my colleague has said, that he the contract signed has. I have asked, whether it a problem gives. he has only answered, that he no time has

words.note: nur stands immediately in front of what it limits: Er hat nur geantwortet (nothing more than answer). Move it and the sentence means something else.

sentences.trap: English backshifts the whole report — he had signed, there was a problem. German keeps what the speaker said: hat unterschrieben, gibt, hat.
sentences.sound: mine ko-LAY-guh hat guh-ZAHKT, das air dayn fair-TRAHK oon-ter-SHREE-ben hat. ikh HAH-buh guh-FRAHKT, op es ine pro-BLAYM gipt. air hat noor guh-ANT-vor-tet, das air KY-nuh tsite hat.
sentences.usage: Passing on an exchange at work to somebody who was not there.

sentences.display: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich meine Eltern besuchen. An deiner Stelle würde ich sofort anrufen. Es wäre besser, wenn wir zusammen fahren würden
sentences.cue: If I had more time, I'd visit my parents. In your place I'd ring straight away. It would be better if we went together
sentences.literal: if I more time had, would I my parents visit. in your place would I immediately call. it would-be better, if we together drive would

words.note: sofort is at once, with no delay at all — stronger than jetzt (L3-M4), which is only now. Ich rufe sofort an.

sentences.trap: Both halves carry a Konjunktiv II: hätte in the wenn clause, würde in the main one. Using the plain present in either half turns the wish into a plan.
sentences.sound: ven ikh mair tsite HET-uh, VUER-duh ikh MY-nuh EL-tern buh-ZOO-khen. an DY-ner SHTEL-uh VUER-duh ikh zo-FORT AN-roo-fen. es VAY-ruh BES-er, ven veer tsoo-ZAM-en FAH-ren VUER-den.
sentences.usage: Advice and a regret in the same breath — the two things L3-M4 opened.

sentences.display: Endlich habe ich wieder Zeit. Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende. Meine Schwester hat mich eingeladen, und ich bin sehr aufgeregt
sentences.cue: I finally have time again. I'm looking forward to the weekend. My sister has invited me, and I'm very excited
sentences.literal: finally have I again time. I gladden me onto the weekend. my sister has me in-loaded, and I am very excited

words.note: endlich carries relief that something waited for has come. schließlich (L2-M10) only orders the events — last in the list, with no feeling in it.

sentences.trap: Endlich is fronted, so the verb comes second and the subject follows it: Endlich habe ich — not Endlich ich habe.
sentences.sound: ENT-likh HAH-buh ikh VEE-der tsite. ikh FROY-uh mikh owf das VOKH-en-en-duh. MY-nuh SHVES-ter hat mikh AYN-guh-lah-den, oont ikh bin zair OWF-guh-raykt.
sentences.usage: The good news at the start of a message to a friend.

sentences.display: Ich habe seit drei Tagen Kopfschmerzen. Plötzlich hatte ich auch Fieber. Deshalb habe ich einen Termin beim Arzt gemacht. Jetzt geht es mir besser
sentences.cue: I've had a headache for three days. Suddenly I had a fever as well. So I made an appointment with the doctor. I feel better now
sentences.literal: I have since three days head-pains. suddenly had I also fever. therefore have I an appointment at-the doctor made. now goes it to-me better

words.note: plötzlich marks the turn in a story and is usually fronted, which sends the verb second: Plötzlich hatte ich Fieber.

sentences.trap: seit keeps the present (habe), while the turn in the story takes a past (hatte). Both live in the same account without disagreeing.
sentences.sound: ikh HAH-buh zyte dry TAH-gen KOPF-shmair-tsen. PLOETS-likh HAT-uh ikh owkh FEE-ber. DES-halp HAH-buh ikh INE-en tair-MEEN bime artst guh-MAKHT. yetst gayt es meer BES-er.
sentences.usage: Telling somebody how an illness went, after it has gone.

sentences.display: Das ist der Vertrag, den ich unterschrieben habe. Wegen des Vertrags muss ich zum Amt gehen. Zum Glück habe ich das Formular schon ausgefüllt
sentences.cue: That's the contract I signed. Because of the contract I have to go to the office. Luckily I've already filled in the form
sentences.literal: that is the contract, which I signed have. because-of the contract must I to-the office go. to-the luck have I the form already out-filled

words.note: A fixed phrase, two words and one meaning, and it is fronted like any other opener: Zum Glück habe ich … Leider (L2-M7) is its opposite.

sentences.trap: Three fronted openers in three sentences — Das, Wegen des Vertrags, Zum Glück — and the verb is second in every one of them.
sentences.sound: das ist dair fair-TRAHK, dayn ikh oon-ter-SHREE-ben HAH-buh. VAY-gen des fair-TRAHKS moos ikh tsoom amt GAY-en. tsoom gluek HAH-buh ikh das for-moo-LAR shone OWS-guh-fuelt.
sentences.usage: The paperwork half of a week, recounted at home.

sentences.display: Bei uns feiert man das Fest im Sommer. Damals haben wir immer zusammen gefeiert. Heute wird das Fest im Dezember gefeiert
sentences.cue: Where I'm from people celebrate the festival in summer. Back then we always celebrated together. Today the festival is celebrated in December
sentences.literal: with us celebrates one the festival in-the summer. back-then have we always together celebrated. today becomes the festival in-the December celebrated

words.note: damals points at a stretch of the past you have already named; dann (L2-M10) points at what comes next. They are not interchangeable.

sentences.trap: The last sentence is L3-M9's present passive, not a past: wird … gefeiert. The past passive is L4-M7's and is not needed here.
sentences.sound: by oons FY-ert man das fest im ZOM-er. DAH-mals HAH-ben veer IM-er tsoo-ZAM-en guh-FY-ert. HOY-tuh virt das fest im day-TSEM-ber guh-FY-ert.
sentences.usage: Saying how something used to be where you are from, without claiming it for anywhere else.

sentences.display: Früher habe ich hier gearbeitet. Dann bin ich nach Berlin gefahren. Kannst du mich morgen anrufen?
sentences.cue: I used to work here. Then I moved to Berlin. Can you ring me tomorrow?
sentences.literal: earlier have I here worked. then am I to Berlin driven. can you me tomorrow call

words.note: The comparative of L1-M5's früh, and on its own it is English's used to: Früher habe ich hier gearbeitet. German has no separate verb for it.

sentences.trap: English needs used to work. German has no such verb — früher plus the ordinary past does the whole job.
sentences.sound: FRUE-er HAH-buh ikh heer guh-AR-buy-tet. dan bin ikh nakh bair-LEEN guh-FAH-ren. kanst doo mikh MOR-gen AN-roo-fen?

variations.display: Früher habe ich hier gearbeitet. Dann bin ich nach Berlin gefahren. Können Sie mich morgen anrufen?
variations.cue: I used to work here. Then I moved to Berlin. Could you ring me tomorrow?
variations.changed: the same story to a stranger — only the address changes, du to Sie

sentences.usage: Your own history in three lines, which is where the level ends.
sentences.mnemonic: Change the address, change nothing else.
